questions.stem: In Dirac notation, \(\langle\psi|\phi\rangle\) is related to \(\langle\phi|\psi\rangle\) by:

explanation.whyCorrect: The inner product is conjugate-symmetric (sesquilinear), which guarantees \(\langle\psi|\psi\rangle\) is real and non-negative.

whyWrong.B: Holds only when the inner product is real.
whyWrong.D: Antisymmetry is not a property of the inner product.

explanation.howToAvoid: Swapping bra and ket always brings a complex conjugate.

questions.stem: For a complete orthonormal basis \(\{|n\rangle\}\), the completeness (closure) relation is:

explanation.whyCorrect: Inserting \(\hat 1 = \sum_n|n\rangle\langle n|\) expands any state: \(|\psi\rangle = \sum_n |n\rangle\langle n|\psi\rangle\).

whyWrong.C: Sums numbers equal to 1 each; it diverges for infinite bases.

explanation.howToModify: Ask for the continuous version \(\int|x\rangle\langle x|dx = \hat 1\).
explanation.howToAvoid: Completeness is an operator identity (ket-bra), orthonormality a number identity (bra-ket).

questions.stem: The operator \(\hat P = |n\rangle\langle n|\) (with \(\langle n|n\rangle = 1\)) satisfies:

explanation.whyCorrect: \(\hat P^2 = |n\rangle\langle n|n\rangle\langle n| = |n\rangle\langle n| = \hat P\): projecting twice is the same as projecting once. \(\hat P\) is also Hermitian with eigenvalues 0 and 1.

whyWrong.B: Involutions such as parity satisfy this.

explanation.trapUsed: Confusing idempotent, nilpotent and involutory operators.
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the eigenvalues of \(\hat P\) (0 and 1).
explanation.howToAvoid: Write out the product and use orthonormality.

questions.stem: The overlap between a position eigenket and a momentum eigenket (one dimension, delta-normalized) is \(\langle x|p\rangle =\):

explanation.whyCorrect: \(\langle x|p\rangle\) is the momentum eigenfunction in position space: \((2\pi\hbar)^{-1/2}e^{ipx/\hbar}\), normalized so that \(\langle p|p'\rangle = \delta(p-p')\).

whyWrong.A: Dimensionally inconsistent: \(x\) and \(p\) have different units.

explanation.howToModify: Ask for \(\langle p|\psi\rangle\) in terms of \(\psi(x)\) (Fourier transform).
explanation.howToAvoid: Plane wave moving with momentum \(p\) has \(+ipx/\hbar\) in position space.

questions.stem: A unitary operator \(\hat U\) (\(\hat U^\dagger\hat U = \hat 1\)) in quantum mechanics:

options.A: changes the norm of the state vector

explanation.whyCorrect: \(\langle U\psi|U\phi\rangle = \langle\psi|U^\dagger U|\phi\rangle = \langle\psi|\phi\rangle\). Time evolution \(e^{-iHt/\hbar}\) is unitary, so total probability is conserved.

whyWrong.B: Eigenvalues of unitary operators lie on the unit circle \(e^{i\theta}\).

explanation.trapUsed: Mixing up Hermitian and unitary properties.
explanation.howToModify: Ask to show that \(e^{i\hat A}\) is unitary when \(\hat A\) is Hermitian.
explanation.howToAvoid: Hermitian ↔ real eigenvalues; Unitary ↔ unit-modulus eigenvalues, norm-preserving.

questions.stem: Which of the following matrices is Hermitian?

explanation.whyCorrect: A Hermitian matrix equals its conjugate transpose: real diagonal and \(A_{12} = A_{21}^*\). Here \(i = (-i)^*\) and diagonal entries are real.

whyWrong.C: Symmetric but not Hermitian: \(A_{12} = i \neq A_{21}^* = -i\).

explanation.howToModify: Ask for the eigenvalues of the Hermitian option (\((3\pm\sqrt5)/2\)).
explanation.howToAvoid: Check: real diagonal, and off-diagonal entries are complex conjugates across the diagonal.
